# Document: vnop_getattr_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_getattr_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_getattr_args

# vnop_getattr_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to see if a kauth-style operation is permitted.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_getattr_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_ACCESS is currently only called on filesystems which mark themselves as doing their authentication remotely (vfs_setauthopaque(), vfs_authopaque()). A VNOP_ACCESS() calldown may come without any preceding VNOP_OPEN().

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_getattr_args/1807228-vp.md): File to authorize action for.
- [action](vnop_getattr_args/1807230-action.md): kauth-style action to be checked for permissions, e.g. KAUTH_VNODE_DELETE.
- [ctx](vnop_getattr_args/1807232-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate action.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_getattr_args/1586271-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_getattr_args/1586319-a_desc.md)
- [a_vap](vnop_getattr_args/1586168-a_vap.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_getattr_args/1585987-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_getxattr_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_getxattr_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_getxattr_args

# vnop_getxattr_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Write data from a mapped file back to disk.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_getxattr_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_PAGEOUT() is called when data from a mapped file needs to be flushed to disk, either because of an msync() call or due to memory pressure. Filesystems are for the most part expected to just call cluster_pageout(). However, if they opt into the VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 flag, then they will be responsible for creating their own UPLs.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_getxattr_args/1807243-vp.md): The vnode for which to page out data.
- [pl](vnop_getxattr_args/1807247-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](vnop_getxattr_args/1807250-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](vnop_getxattr_args/1807253-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [size](vnop_getxattr_args/1807254-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [flags](vnop_getxattr_args/1807257-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](vnop_getxattr_args/1807260-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_getxattr_args/1807243-vp
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_getxattr_args/1807243-vp

# vp

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The vnode for which to page out data.

## See Also

### Fields

- [pl](1807247-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](1807250-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](1807253-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [size](1807254-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [flags](1807257-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](1807260-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

- [f_offset](1807253-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [flags](1807257-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](1807260-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

- [size](1807254-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.

# vnop_getxattr_desc

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Global Variable  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Write data from a mapped file back to disk.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnodeop_desc vnop_getxattr_desc;
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_PAGEOUT() is called when data from a mapped file needs to be flushed to disk, either because of an msync() call or due to memory pressure. Filesystems are for the most part expected to just call cluster_pageout(). However, if they opt into the VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 flag, then they will be responsible for creating their own UPLs.

The vnode for which to page out data.

UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.

Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.

Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.

Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.

UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.

Context to authenticate for pageout request.

# vnop_inactive_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to get the pathname represented by a symbolic link.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_inactive_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_READLINK() gets the path stored in a symbolic link; it is called by namei() and the readlink() system call.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_inactive_args/1807261-vp.md): Symbolic link to read from.
- [uio](vnop_inactive_args/1807265-uio.md): Destination information for link path.

# Document: vnop_link_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_link_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_link_args

# vnop_link_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to delete a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_link_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_REMOVE is called to remove a file from a filesystem's namespace, for example by unlink(). It can operate on regular files, named pipes, special files, and in some cases on directories.

## Topics

### Fields

- [dvp](vnop_link_args/1807270-dvp.md): Directory in which to delete a file.
- [vp](vnop_link_args/1807271-vp.md): The file to delete.
- [cnp](vnop_link_args/1807272-cnp.md): Filename information.
- [ctx](vnop_link_args/1807273-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for fsync request.

# vnop_listxattr_desc

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Kind:** Global Variable  
**Availability:** macOS 10.4+

Remove extended file attributes.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnodeop_desc vnop_listxattr_desc;
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The vnode from which to remove extended attributes.

Which attribute to delete.

XATTR_NOSECURITY: bypass security-checking.

Context to authenticate for attribute delete request.

## See Also

# Document: vnop_mkdir_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_mkdir_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_mkdir_args

# vnop_mkdir_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to rename a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_mkdir_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_RENAME() will only be called with a source and target on the same volume.

## Topics

### Fields

- [fdvp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807293-fdvp.md): Directory in which source file resides.
- [fvp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807295-fvp.md): File being renamed.
- [fcnp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807297-fcnp.md): Name information for source file.
- [tdvp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807300-tdvp.md): Directory file is being moved to.
- [tvp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807304-tvp.md): Existing file with same name as target, should one exist.
- [tcnp](vnop_mkdir_args/1807305-tcnp.md): Name information for target path.
- [ctx](vnop_mkdir_args/1807306-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for rename request.

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_mknod_args

# vnop_mknod_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to create a whiteout.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_mknod_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Whiteouts are used to support the union filesystem, whereby one filesystem is mounted "transparently" on top of another. A whiteout in the upper layer of a union mount is a "deletion" of a file in the lower layer; lookups will catch the whiteout and fail, setting ISWHITEOUT in the componentname structure, even if an underlying file of the same name exists. The whiteout vnop is used for creation, deletion, and checking whether a directory supports whiteouts (see flags). also support the LOOKUP flag, which is used to test whether a directory supports whiteouts.

## Topics

### Fields

- [dvp](vnop_mknod_args/1807307-dvp.md): Directory in which to create.
- [cnp](vnop_mknod_args/1807310-cnp.md): Name information for whiteout.
- [flags](vnop_mknod_args/1807313-flags.md): CREATE: create a whiteout. LOOKUP: check whether a directory supports whiteouts, DELETE: remove a whiteout.
- [ctx](vnop_mknod_args/1807317-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate whiteout creation.

# Document: vnop_mmap_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_mmap_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_mmap_args

# vnop_mmap_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to invalidate all open file descriptors for a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_mmap_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

This function is typically called as part of a TTY revoke, but can also be used on regular files. Most filesystems simply use nop_revoke(), which calls vn_revoke(), as their revoke vnop implementation.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_mmap_args/1807320-vp.md): The vnode to revoke.
- [flags](vnop_mmap_args/1807322-flags.md): Unused.
- [ctx](vnop_mmap_args/1807323-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for revoke request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_mmap_args/1585994-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_mmap_args/1586032-a_desc.md)
- [a_fflags](vnop_mmap_args/1586013-a_fflags.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_mmap_args/1585977-a_vp.md)

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_mnomap_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_mnomap_args

# vnop_mnomap_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Notify a filesystem that a file is being mmap-ed.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_mnomap_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_MMAP is an advisory calldown to say that the system is mmap-ing a file.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_mnomap_args/1807325-vp.md): The vnode being mmapped.
- [flags](vnop_mnomap_args/1807326-flags.md): Memory protection: PROT_READ, PROT_WRITE, PROT_EXEC.
- [ctx](vnop_mnomap_args/1807329-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for mmap request.

- [a_context](vnop_mnomap_args/1586101-a_context.md)

# Document: vnop_offtoblk_args

# vnop_offtoblk_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to convert a logical block number to a file offset.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_offtoblk_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_BLKTOOFF() converts a logical block to a file offset in bytes. That offset can be passed to VNOP_BLOCKMAP(), then, to get a physical block number--buf_strategy() does this.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_offtoblk_args/1807337-vp.md): The vnode for which to convert a logical block to an offset.
- [lblkno](vnop_offtoblk_args/1807345-lblkno.md): Logical block number to turn into offset.
- [offset](vnop_offtoblk_args/1807353-offset.md): Destination for file offset.

### Instance Properties

- [a_desc](vnop_offtoblk_args/1585993-a_desc.md)
- [a_lblkno](vnop_offtoblk_args/1586293-a_lblkno.md)
- [a_offset](vnop_offtoblk_args/1586020-a_offset.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_offtoblk_args/1586202-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_open_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_open_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_open_args

# vnop_open_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to create a special file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_open_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The mknod vnop is used to create character and block device files, named pipe (FIFO) files, and named sockets. The newly created file should be returned with an iocount which will be dropped by the caller. A VNOP_MKNOD() call can come down without a preceding VNOP_OPEN().

## Topics

### Fields

- [dvp](vnop_open_args/1807362-dvp.md): Directory in which to create the special file.
- [vpp](vnop_open_args/1807367-vpp.md): Destination for newly created vnode.
- [cnp](vnop_open_args/1807373-cnp.md): Name information for new file.
- [vap](vnop_open_args/1807377-vap.md): Attributes for new file, including type.
- [ctx](vnop_open_args/1807385-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate node creation.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_open_args/1586175-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_open_args/1586128-a_desc.md)
- [a_mode](vnop_open_args/1586035-a_mode.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_open_args/1586115-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_pagein_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_pagein_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_pagein_args

# vnop_pagein_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Pre-allocate space for a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_pagein_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_ALLOCATE() changes the amount of backing store set aside to a file. It can be used to either shrink or grow a file. If the file shrinks, its ubc size will be modified accordingly, but if it grows, then the ubc size is unchanged; space is set aside without being actively used by the file. VNOP_ALLOCATE() is currently only called as part of the F_PREALLOCATE fcntl.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_pagein_args/1807403-vp.md): The vnode for which to preallocate space.
- [length](vnop_pagein_args/1807414-length.md): Desired preallocated file length.
- [flags](vnop_pagein_args/1807426-flags.md): PREALLOCATE: preallocate allocation blocks. ALLOCATECONTIG: allocate contigious space. ALLOCATEALL: allocate all requested space or no space at all. FREEREMAINDER: deallocate allocated but unfilled blocks. ALLOCATEFROMPEOF: allocate from the physical eof. ALLOCATEFROMVOL: allocate from the volume offset.
- [bytesallocated](vnop_pagein_args/1807437-bytesallocated.md): Additional bytes set aside for file. Set to 0 if none are allocated OR if the file is contracted.
- [offset](vnop_pagein_args/1807450-offset.md): Hint for where to find free blocks.
- [ctx](vnop_pagein_args/1807464-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for allocation request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_pagein_args/1586104-a_context.md)

# vp

**Framework:** Kernel

The vnode for which to preallocate space.

## See Also

### Fields

- [length](1807414-length.md): Desired preallocated file length.
- [flags](1807426-flags.md): PREALLOCATE: preallocate allocation blocks. ALLOCATECONTIG: allocate contigious space. ALLOCATEALL: allocate all requested space or no space at all. FREEREMAINDER: deallocate allocated but unfilled blocks. ALLOCATEFROMPEOF: allocate from the physical eof. ALLOCATEFROMVOL: allocate from the volume offset.
- [bytesallocated](1807437-bytesallocated.md): Additional bytes set aside for file. Set to 0 if none are allocated OR if the file is contracted.
- [offset](1807450-offset.md): Hint for where to find free blocks.
- [ctx](1807464-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for allocation request.

# Document: vnop_pageout_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_pageout_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_pageout_args

# vnop_pageout_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Pull file data into memory.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_pageout_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_PAGEIN() is called by when a process faults on data mapped from a file or when madvise() demands pre-fetching. It is conceptually somewhat similar to VNOP_READ(). Filesystems are typically expected to call cluster_pagein() to handle the labor of mapping and committing the UPL.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_pageout_args/1807482-vp.md): The vnode for which to page in data.
- [pl](vnop_pageout_args/1807490-pl.md): UPL describing pages needing to be paged in.
- [pl_offset](vnop_pageout_args/1807495-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL at which to start placing data.
- [f_offset](vnop_pageout_args/1807502-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged in.
- [size](vnop_pageout_args/1807509-size.md): Amount of data to page in (in bytes).
- [flags](vnop_pageout_args/1807514-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](vnop_pageout_args/1807517-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pagein request.

# Document: vnop_pathconf_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_pathconf_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_pathconf_args

# vnop_pathconf_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Release filesystem-internal resources for a vnode.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_pathconf_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_RECLAIM() is called as part of the process of recycling a vnode. During a reclaim routine, a filesystem should remove a vnode from its hash and deallocate any resources allocated to that vnode. VFS guarantees that when VNOP_RECLAIM() is called, there are no more iocount references on a vnode (though there may still be usecount references--these are invalidated by the reclaim) and that no more will be granted. This means in practice that there will be no filesystem calls on the vnode being reclaimed until the reclaim has finished and the vnode has been reused.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_pathconf_args/1807521-vp.md): The vnode to reclaim.
- [ctx](vnop_pathconf_args/1807524-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for reclaim.

# Document: vnop_read_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_read_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_read_args

# vnop_read_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to set vnode attributes.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_read_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Supported attributes ("Yes, I am setting this attribute.") are set with VATTR_SET_SUPPORTED. Requested attributes are checked with VATTR_IS_ACTIVE. Attribute values are accessed directly through structure fields. VNOP_SETATTR() is the core of the KPI function vnode_setattr(), which is used by chmod(), chown(), truncate(), and many others. A VNOP_SETATTR() call may come without any preceding VNOP_OPEN().

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_read_args/1807536-vp.md): The vnode whose attributes to set.
- [vap](vnop_read_args/1807548-vap.md): Container for which attributes are to be set and their desired values, as well as for the filesystem to return information about which attributes were successfully set.
- [ctx](vnop_read_args/1807562-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate request for attribute change.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_read_args/1586075-a_context.md)

- [a_ioflag](vnop_read_args/1586062-a_ioflag.md)
- [a_uio](vnop_read_args/1586244-a_uio.md)

# vnop_readdir_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to create a symbolic link.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_readdir_args {
    ...
};
```

## Topics

### Fields

- [If](vnop_readdir_args/1807590-if.md): VNOP_SYMLINK() is successful, the new file should be returned with an iocount which will be dropped by the caller. VFS does not ensure that the target path will have a length shorter than the max symlink length for the filesystem.
- [dvp](vnop_readdir_args/1807603-dvp.md): Parent directory for new symlink file.
- [vpp](vnop_readdir_args/1807609-vpp.md)
- [cnp](vnop_readdir_args/1807615-cnp.md): Name information for new symlink.
- [vap](vnop_readdir_args/1807617-vap.md): Attributes for symlink.
- [target](vnop_readdir_args/1807620-target.md): Path for symlink to store; for "ln -s /var/vardir linktovardir", "target" would be "/var/vardir"
- [ctx](vnop_readdir_args/1807622-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for symlink request.

# If

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

VNOP_SYMLINK() is successful, the new file should be returned with an iocount which will be dropped by the caller. VFS does not ensure that the target path will have a length shorter than the max symlink length for the filesystem.

# Document: vnop_readdirattr_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_readdirattr_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_readdirattr_args

# vnop_readdirattr_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to enumerate directory entries.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_readdirattr_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_READDIR() packs a buffer with "struct dirent" directory entry representations as described by the "getdirentries" manual page.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807627-vp.md): Directory to enumerate.
- [uio](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807633-uio.md): Destination information for resulting direntries.
- [flags](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807637-flags.md): VNODE_READDIR_EXTENDED, VNODE_READDIR_REQSEEKOFF, VNODE_READDIR_SEEKOFF32: Apple-internal flags.
- [eofflag](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807642-eofflag.md): Should be set to 1 if the end of the directory has been reached.
- [numdirent](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807646-numdirent.md): Should be set to number of entries written into buffer.
- [ctx](vnop_readdirattr_args/1807650-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for readdir request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_actualcount](vnop_readdirattr_args/1586012-a_actualcount.md)

# Document: vnop_readlink_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_readlink_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_readlink_args

# vnop_readlink_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to get file attributes for many files in a directory at once.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_readlink_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_READDIRATTR() packs a buffer with file attributes, as if the results of many "getattrlist" calls.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_readlink_args/1807660-vp.md): Directory in which to enumerate entries' attributes.
- [alist](vnop_readlink_args/1807668-alist.md): Which attributes are wanted for each directory entry.
- [uio](vnop_readlink_args/1807675-uio.md): Destination information for resulting attributes.
- [maxcount](vnop_readlink_args/1807683-maxcount.md): Maximum count of files to get attributes for.
- [options](vnop_readlink_args/1807690-options.md): FSOPT_NOFOLLOW: do not follow symbolic links. FSOPT_NOINMEMUPDATE: do not use data which have been updated since an inode was loaded into memory.
- [newstate](vnop_readlink_args/1807697-newstate.md): The "newstate" should be set to a value which changes if the contents of a directory change through an addition or deletion but stays the same otherwise.
- [eofflag](vnop_readlink_args/1807701-eofflag.md): Should be set to 1 if the end of the directory has been reached.
- [actualcount](vnop_readlink_args/1807705-actualcount.md): Should be set to number of files whose attributes were written into buffer.
- [ctx](vnop_readlink_args/1807709-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for readdirattr request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_readlink_args/1586279-a_context.md)

- [a_uio](vnop_readlink_args/1586135-a_uio.md)

# Document: vnop_reclaim_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_reclaim_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_reclaim_args

# vnop_reclaim_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Notify a filesystem that the last usecount (persistent reference) on a vnode has been dropped.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_reclaim_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_INACTVE() gives a filesystem a chance to aggressively release resources assocated with a vnode, perhaps even to call vnode_recycle(), but no action is prescribed; it is acceptable for VNOP_INACTIVE to be a no-op and to defer all reclamation until VNOP_RECLAIM(). VNOP_INACTVE() will not be called on a vnode if no persistent reference is ever taken; an important example is a stat(), which takes an iocount, reads its data, and drops that iocount.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_reclaim_args/1807717-vp.md): The vnode which is now inactive.
- [ctx](vnop_reclaim_args/1807721-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for inactive message.

# Document: vnop_rename_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_rename_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_rename_args

# vnop_rename_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to create a hardlink to a file.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_rename_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

See "man 2 link".

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_rename_args/1807753-vp.md): File to link to.
- [dvp](vnop_rename_args/1807756-dvp.md): Directory in which to create the link.
- [cnp](vnop_rename_args/1807759-cnp.md): Filename information for new link.
- [ctx](vnop_rename_args/1807761-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for link request.

# Document: vnop_revoke_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_revoke_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_revoke_args

# vnop_revoke_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to atomically exchange the data of two files.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_revoke_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_EXCHANGE() is currently only called by the exchangedata() system call. It will only be applied to files on the same volume.

## Topics

### Fields

- [fvp](vnop_revoke_args/1807765-fvp.md): First vnode.
- [tvp](vnop_revoke_args/1807769-tvp.md): Second vnode.
- [options](vnop_revoke_args/1807772-options.md): Unused.
- [ctx](vnop_revoke_args/1807776-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for exchangedata request.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_revoke_args/1586055-a_context.md)

- [a_vp](vnop_revoke_args/1586122-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_rmdir_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_rmdir_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_rmdir_args

# vnop_rmdir_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to create a directory.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_rmdir_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The newly created directory should be returned with an iocount which will be dropped by the caller.

## Topics

### Fields

- [dvp](vnop_rmdir_args/1807781-dvp.md): Directory in which to create new directory.
- [vpp](vnop_rmdir_args/1807786-vpp.md): Destination for pointer to new directory's vnode.
- [cnp](vnop_rmdir_args/1807788-cnp.md): Name information for new directory.
- [vap](vnop_rmdir_args/1807790-vap.md): Attributes for new directory.
- [ctx](vnop_rmdir_args/1807793-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for mkdir request.

### Instance Properties

# Document: vnop_searchfs_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_searchfs_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_searchfs_args

# vnop_searchfs_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Write data from a mapped file back to disk.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_searchfs_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_PAGEOUT() is called when data from a mapped file needs to be flushed to disk, either because of an msync() call or due to memory pressure. Filesystems are for the most part expected to just call cluster_pageout(). However, if they opt into the VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 flag, then they will be responsible for creating their own UPLs.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_searchfs_args/1807795-vp.md): The vnode for which to page out data.
- [pl](vnop_searchfs_args/1807798-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](vnop_searchfs_args/1807800-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](vnop_searchfs_args/1807802-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [size](vnop_searchfs_args/1807803-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [flags](vnop_searchfs_args/1807804-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](vnop_searchfs_args/1807805-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

# Document: vp

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_searchfs_args/1807795-vp
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_searchfs_args/1807795-vp

# vp

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

The vnode for which to page out data.

## See Also

### Fields

- [pl](1807798-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](1807800-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](1807802-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [size](1807803-size.md): Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.
- [flags](1807804-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](1807805-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

- [flags](1807804-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](1807805-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

# size

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel

Amount of data to page out (in bytes). Under VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2, this represents the size of the range to be considered. The fileystem is free to extend or shrink the specified range to better fit its blocking model as long as the page at 'pl_offset' is included.

## See Also

### Fields

- [vp](1807795-vp.md): The vnode for which to page out data.
- [pl](1807798-pl.md): UPL describing pages needed to be paged out. If UPL is NULL, then it means the filesystem has opted into VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, which means that it will create and operate on its own UPLs as opposed to relying on the one passed down into the filesystem. This means that the filesystem must be responsible for N cluster_pageout calls for N dirty ranges in the UPL.
- [pl_offset](1807800-pl_offset.md): Offset in UPL from which to start paging out data. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this is the offset in the range specified that must be paged out if the associated page is dirty.
- [f_offset](1807802-f_offset.md): Offset in file of data needing to be paged out. Under the new VFC_VFSVNOP_PAGEOUTV2 semantics, this represents the offset in the file where we should start looking for dirty pages.
- [flags](1807804-flags.md): UPL-style flags: UPL_IOSYNC, UPL_NOCOMMIT, UPL_NORDAHEAD, UPL_VNODE_PAGER, UPL_MSYNC. Filesystems should generally leave it to the cluster layer to handle these flags. See the memory_object_types.h header in the kernel framework if interested.
- [ctx](1807805-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for pageout request.

# Document: vnop_setattr_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_setattr_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_setattr_args

# vnop_setattr_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to get vnode attributes.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_setattr_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

Supported attributes ("Yes, I am returning this information") are set with VATTR_SET_SUPPORTED. Which attributes have been requested is checked with VATTR_IS_ACTIVE. Attributes are returned with VATTR_RETURN. It is through VNOP_GETATTR that routines like stat() get their information. A VNOP_GETATTR() calldown may come without any preceding VNOP_OPEN().

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_setattr_args/1807806-vp.md): The vnode whose attributes to get.
- [vap](vnop_setattr_args/1807807-vap.md): Container for which attributes are requested, which attributes are supported by the filesystem, and attribute values.
- [ctx](vnop_setattr_args/1807809-ctx.md): Context against which to authenticate request for attributes.

### Instance Properties

- [a_context](vnop_setattr_args/1585985-a_context.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_setattr_args/1586108-a_desc.md)
- [a_vap](vnop_setattr_args/1585999-a_vap.md)
- [a_vp](vnop_setattr_args/1586313-a_vp.md)

# Document: vnop_strategy_args

Source path: documentation/kernel/vnop_strategy_args
Canonical source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel/vnop_strategy_args

# vnop_strategy_args

**Interface language:** Objective-C

**Framework:** Kernel  
**Availability:** macOS 10.6+

Call down to a filesystem to get information about the on-disk layout of a file region.

## Declaration

```objectivec
struct vnop_strategy_args {
    ...
};
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

VNOP_BLOCKMAP() returns the information required to pass a request for a contiguous region down to a device's strategy routine.

## Topics

### Fields

- [vp](vnop_strategy_args/1807814-vp.md): The vnode for which to get on-disk information.
- [foffset](vnop_strategy_args/1807816-foffset.md): Offset (in bytes) at which region starts.
- [size](vnop_strategy_args/1807819-size.md): Size of region.
- [bpn](vnop_strategy_args/1807821-bpn.md): Destination for physical block number at which region begins on disk.
- [run](vnop_strategy_args/1807823-run.md): Destination for number of bytes which can be found contiguously on-disk before first discontinuity.
- [poff](vnop_strategy_args/1807826-poff.md): Currently unused.
- [flags](vnop_strategy_args/1807828-flags.md): VNODE_READ: request is for a read. VNODE_WRITE: request is for a write.
- [ctx](vnop_strategy_args/1807831-ctx.md): Context to authenticate for blockmap request; currently often set to NULL.

### Instance Properties

- [a_bp](vnop_strategy_args/1586169-a_bp.md)
- [a_desc](vnop_strategy_args/1586234-a_desc.md)
